newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht recovers but still vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht recovers but still vulnerable.

text.p: The Thai baht recovered some ground on Thursday as players turned wary of selling it down after the previous day's joint intervention by the central banks of Thailand and Singapore.
"The hedge funds are still buying the rumours the same as yesterday but the force is lesser now since the Bank of Thailand and other banks came in," a Siam Commercial Bank dealer in Bangkok said.
Dealers said activity had subsided in the spot baht market but forwards were shooting up due to a severe shortage of funds after Wednesday's aggressive baht sales by speculative funds.
The baht was quoted at 25.790-25.840 to the dollar at 0415 GMT against 25.910/25.940 earlier and 26.330-26/430 late on Wednesday. The Bank of Thailand (BOT) set the mid-rate at 25.81.
"Everybody's hitting the forwards. I think they're just squeezing the short-term liquidity. Tom/next is at 65/100 -- it's like trading the one-year," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
Dealers said there had been no signs of central bank intervention on Thursday.
"They (the BOT) have informed banks in Thailand not to quote to offshore parties for tom/next. There's no need for them to intervene," another Singapore-based dealer said.
"Everybody's just trying to fight for survival, they're just scrambling for funds," he added.
Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday that Thailand had been and would continue to be successful in defending the baht.
"We have support from all our friends," he told reporters as he left a seminar in Tokyo.

The BOT and Singapore's de facto central bank, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), said in a statement on Wednesday that they had taken joint action to stem excessive speculative activities in the baht.
It was the first joint action confirmed by the two central banks.
In Indonesia, the rupiah remained under pressure after being aggressively sold overnight on false rumours of unrest in Jakarta during the campaign for the May 29 election.
Spot rupiah was at 2,438.50/39.50 at 0415 GMT after finding some support at the 2,439.0 level, compared with an opening of 2,433.0/44.0.
Swap rates rose broadly on foreign buying, dealers said.
They said a carry-forward effect from Wednesday, coupled with the ongoing jitters in the Thai market, hit the rupiah, triggering more stop-loss dollar buying.
The rupiah tumbled to a low of 2,445 in London overnight on false rumours of violence and arson at a police station in Jakarta, but it later recovered to 2,435.
Dealers said stop-loss limits were triggered in Singapore and London late on Wednesday after the rupiah was hit by the rumours.
One major local bank dealer said swap points jumped in early Thursday trading as offshore operators were squeezed on the forward side.
"Offshore players going long on dollars have to buy swaps for hedging or to get the rupiah financing, driving swap rates up across the board," the dealer said.
The Malaysian ringgit staged a partial recovery but continued to look vulnerable after foreign funds dumped the currency on Wednesday due to spillover fears over Thailand.
"Today the market is caught a bit long so they're selling dollars but it looks supported around 2.5160," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said players would also be wary of pushing the ringgit down again after Bank Negara's aggressive intervention in London markets overnight.
"Negara was in aggressively around the 2.5250 level yesterday in London. They probably sold more than $1 billion," he said.
A European bank dealer in Singapore pegged the amount sold by the Malaysian central bank at around $700 million.
The ringgit was at 2.5176/86 to the dollar at 0415 GMT against 2.5240/50 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. It had fallen to as low as 2.5260, its lowest level since January 3.
The Singapore dollar was firm in the face of its neighbours' woes, but dealers said potential "safe-haven" flows to the currency were being dampened by fears of MAS intervention.
"The MAS has been supporting the (U.S) dollar at the 1.4320 level. I don't know why they want to hold it here since the dollar/yen has come off so much," a U.S. bank dealer said.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), James Mclean in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore
